text:
aj: Quick sync — spike showed two viable patterns for private CP connectivity: per-tenant /24s (full subnet per customer) vs regional private endpoint + host routing. Thoughts?
maria: Per-tenant subnets buy us IP isolation and easier firewall rules, but it's a big IP footprint. We already hit ENI limits for the largest accounts.
lee: Agreed. Also ops cost to manage NACLs+route tables per tenant grows linearly. How many tenants are we planning for per region? 
sophie: For enterprise alpha we expect ~300 tenants/region over 3 years. /24s will exhaust private space fast unless we do IPv6.
aj: Right — alternative was private endpoint with SNI/Host header routing at the regional relay. That keeps address space small but requires us to terminate TLS or SNI-proxy.
maria: Terminating TLS in our regional relay is a compliance concern for some customers. SNI passthrough + host-based L4 routing is possible but limits observability (can't do token-level tracing before routing).
lee: Another middle ground: route by TCP destination port per-tenant, but that's brittle and conflicts with client expectations.
sophie: We also discussed mTLS for CP->agent auth. If relay does TLS termination we must re-establish mTLS to agent or carry client cert info forward. That gets messy.
aj: From the spike: performance diff is minimal under our workload. Main tradeoffs: IP space + ops vs cert surface + observability.
infra-bot: Note: peering quotas alert will trigger at ~190 peers in us-west-2 (link: https://aws.amazon.com/peering-quotas)
maria: Could we do a hybrid: big customers get /24s (dedicated IPs) and small ones go to the regional endpoint? Would simplify migrations.
lee: Hybrid seems pragmatic. Need a robust cutover: move route table entries and update client bootstrap. Also ensure tenant cert rotation doesn't break.
sophie: Implementation note — operator needs an API to assign tenancy mode. Also a migration playbook: sample commands:
```
# assign tenant to dedicated subnet
redwoodctl tenant assign-subnet --tenant-id t-123 --subnet 10.0.200.0/24
# move back to regional endpoint
redwoodctl tenant set-endpoint-mode --tenant-id t-123 --mode regional
```
aj: +1. Also add an audit log entry every time we change mode.
maria: For TLS flows we should prefer preserving end-to-end mTLS for enterprise customers by advertising TLS passthrough for those tenants and using dedicated subnets. For regional mode we accept proxy termination for now.
lee: Ops checklist: ENI limits, Route53 private zones per tenant, security group sprawl, peering quotas if we ever go with per-tenant peering.
sophie: I'll draft an RFC addendum with migration steps, operator API surface, and an auth flow diagram showing when relay terminates vs passes through.
aj: Thanks — once Sophie posts the RFC I'll link and we can schedule a 30m architecture check-in.
infra-bot: Reminder: run peering-cost-estimator after RFC published.
maria: sgtm :thumbsup:
